title: Pulse-step: endorsement-gated knowledge integrity, language-agnostic spec
desc: Portable specification of the pulse-step mechanism: after a unit of work an actor must ENDORSE one existing lesson by quoting a verbatim fragment of it, and the endorsement both clears the work-debt and reorders the corpus. Implementation-neutral -- data model, algorithm, anti-gaming rules, porting notes and the production failure modes. Written so it can be built in any language or harness, not only in wkappbot.
steps: PROBLEM: an agent that merely READS its lessons does not apply them, and every harness that tries to fix this by mandating a read gets exactly that -- the file is opened, the counter advances, the behaviour does not change. A READ IS A COUNT; AN ENDORSEMENT IS A CLAIM. The pulse-step mechanism replaces the read requirement with an ENDORSEMENT requirement: after finishing a unit of work, the actor must point at ONE specific existing lesson and assert that THIS lesson carried THIS work. That assertion is checkable in a way a read never is, because it names a target and the target has content the actor must have understood in order to pick it correctly. Nothing in the design depends on a particular language or runtime.

THE ONE INVARIANT, and everything else is derived from it: THE PAYMENT MUST BE IMPOSSIBLE TO MAKE WITHOUT HAVING READ THE CONTENT. A payment that can be produced from the gate's own error message is not a payment, it is a form to fill in. Concretely, the endorsement is keyed by a VERBATIM FRAGMENT of the target step's text -- not an index, not a title, not an id. An index is guessable (1, 2, 3); a title is printed in every listing; a fragment of step BODY can only be produced by someone who opened it. Measured in the origin system: while index-addressing was permitted, actors paid with a bare number and the gate was satisfied though nothing had been read. The fix was to DELETE the index form, not to warn about it.

DATA MODEL, portable to any language. Three entities. (1) LESSON -- an ordered collection of STEPS, each step free text whose identity comes from its CONTENT, never its position, because endorsement REORDERS the collection. (2) LEDGER -- append-only records {actor, lesson_id, step_fingerprint, timestamp, rationale}; the rationale is one sentence on why this lesson applied HERE, and it is what makes a hollow payment visible. (3) DEBT -- a per-actor flag, set when a unit of work completes, cleared only by a ledger record whose timestamp is AFTER the debt was set. That ordering requirement is load-bearing: a payment made before the work would turn the mechanism into a warm-up ritual.

THE ALGORITHM, pseudocode, no language-specific constructs. on WORK_COMPLETED(actor): debt[actor] = true. on NEXT_WORK_REQUESTED(actor): if debt[actor] then REFUSE, naming the payment form. on ENDORSE(actor, lesson_id, fragment, rationale): resolve the lesson; find the step whose text CONTAINS fragment; if zero matches REFUSE as no-match, if two or more REFUSE as ambiguous; append the ledger record; move that step toward the FRONT of its collection; debt[actor] = false. THE REORDERING IS NOT DECORATION -- it is how the corpus learns. A step endorsed often rises to where the next reader meets it first; one never endorsed sinks. The collection acquires a relevance gradient with nobody curating it.

ANTI-GAMING, each rule bought with a measured failure. (a) REFUSE A BARE INDEX, per the invariant. (b) REFUSE A PAYMENT AGAINST A LESSON THE ACTOR JUST WROTE -- otherwise the actor authors a step and endorses it, a closed loop certifying nothing. (c) REQUIRE THE FRAGMENT TO MATCH EXACTLY ONE STEP; an ambiguous fragment lets the actor aim at nothing in particular. (d) THE REFUSAL MESSAGE MUST NOT CONTAIN A USABLE FRAGMENT -- a gate that quotes the step it wants has handed over the answer. (e) TREAT A DUPLICATED RATIONALE AS UNPAID: the same sentence twice for the same step is a copy, not a thought.

PORTING NOTES. The mechanism needs three primitives every mainstream language has: a keyed store for lesson collections, an append-only log, and a hook that fires on work completion. In a shell harness the hook is a pre-command and post-command trap; in an agent framework it is tool-call middleware; in CI it is a post-job step. STORAGE: anything with stable per-step text -- JSON, YAML, or a directory of markdown files one step per file. Do NOT persist the step index as identity; persist the text and fingerprint it, so reordering never invalidates history. CONCURRENCY: the ledger is append-only so concurrent actors need no lock, but DEBT is mutable per-actor state and does -- one writer per actor, a file or a row, is enough. FAILURE POSTURE: if the ledger cannot be read, REFUSE rather than allow. A gate that fails open is not a gate.

FAILURE MODES SEEN IN PRODUCTION, design against them from day one. THE SELF-SEALING LESSON: if the gate ALSO requires the endorsed lesson to clear a quality score, a lesson that decays below the floor becomes unendorsable, and when it is the only lesson covering that work the actor is locked out with no legal move. Remedy: let the actor name a DIFFERENT healthy lesson; never lower the floor; and never let the only escape be editing the very thing the gate protects. THE FORMAT RATCHET: if steps must match a rigid shape, every step written before the shape existed becomes unpayable, silently shrinking the payable surface until the gate is unsatisfiable -- so validate shape on WRITE, never on ENDORSE. THE RITUAL DRIFT: actors converge on the cheapest valid endorsement rather than the truest one; the rationale field is the only defence, so sample rationales periodically, and if they read interchangeably the gate has already become a form.

WHY THE MECHANISM IS WORTH THE FRICTION, stated plainly so a porter can judge it. It costs the actor one extra call per unit of work and it buys three things nothing else in a harness buys. FIRST, it converts a corpus from storage into a ranked working set at zero curation cost, because endorsement is the only signal that correlates with a lesson having actually been used. SECOND, it produces an audit trail that answers WHICH lesson governed a piece of work, which no read-log can answer. THIRD, and this is the one that justifies it, the act of choosing a fragment forces the actor to re-read at the moment of maximum relevance -- immediately after doing the work -- rather than at session start when nothing is concrete yet. If you port only one property, port that timing: the payment must fall AFTER the work, never before.

requirements.cmd: endorse with a verbatim fragment of an existing step
requirements.expect: accepted, step moves toward the front, debt cleared

requirements.cmd: endorse with a bare numeric index
requirements.expect: refused, an index is guessable without reading

requirements.cmd: request new work while debt is set
requirements.expect: refused, and the refusal must NOT quote a usable fragment
